label: Work by a variable force
subgoals: Write W = integral of F(x) dx

slice.rule: When a force varies with position along a line, the work it does moving an object from $x = a$ to $x = b$ is $W = \int_a^b F(x)\,dx$: force times a tiny displacement, summed.

label: Power-law forces
subgoals: Compute work to infinity when finite

slice.rule: A force $F(x) = kx^n$ gives $W = k\dfrac{b^{n+1} - a^{n+1}}{n+1}$ for $n \neq -1$. Inverse-square forces ($n = -2$) do finite work even out to infinity, which is why escape velocity exists.

label: Spring work
subgoals: Find k from a given stretch
Integrate from one stretch to another

slice.rule: Hooke's law gives $F(x) = kx$ for a spring stretched $x$ past its natural length, so the work to stretch it from $a$ to $b$ is $W = \tfrac{1}{2}k(b^2 - a^2)$. Find $k$ first from any force–stretch pair you are given.

examples.item: A 10 N force holds a spring 0.2 m stretched; work from 0 to 0.5 m
Same spring, from 0.2 m to 0.4 m

slice.note: Measure $x$ from the natural length, not from the current stretched position.
